title: The Rocky Horror Picture Show Podcast Episode
summary: Hosts Josh and Chuck cover The Rocky Horror Picture Show, starting with their personal viewing histories and a Tim Curry anecdote. They trace its origins from Richard O'Brien's songs and the 1973 London stage production of The Rocky Horror Show (Royal Court Theater, Tim Curry as Frank-N-Furter, Sue Blaine's costumes), its move to Los Angeles with meat Loaf, and the 1975 film made on a shoestring budget with 20th Century Fox and a poor reception. They describe how the midnight screenings at the Waverly Theater starting in 1976 spawned audience participation, callouts, props, and shadow casting. They discuss the film's gender-fluid themes and the 2016 remake with Laverne Cox, Susan Sarandon's illness, Patricia Quinn lip-syncing, Elvis being floated as Eddie, the sequel Shock Treatment, and Easter eggs. The episode closes with a year-end sign-off and a listener mail about Oxfordian theories of Shakespeare's authorship.
